newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debts mixed, Russia plays catch-up.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debts mixed, Russia plays catch-up.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were generally lower on the back of sliding U.S. Treasuries, but Russia papers scored hefty gains in a belated move to keep pace with the rest of the market, traders said.
"Russia has not participated in the rally since beginning of the year," said the head of trading in a U.S. investment house. "It is catching up."
The absence of alarming news on Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health might have given the debt market a respite, the trader said.
In January 2-15, Russia debt prices fell 3.34 percent, while the broad Brady index rose 2.4 percent, according to J.P. Morgan Emerging Markets Bond Index.
Russia dollar Vnesh rose 5/8 to 78-5/8, and Deutschemark Vnesh jumped 1-3/8 to 83-5/8.
Among the Latin Bradies, Mexico Bradies firmed on followthrough buying from Wednesday.
"The debt payback was very positive for the sentiment," another trader said.
Mexico Discount rose 3/4 to 89-7/8 and Mexico UMS-26 gained 5/8 to 108.00.
But the best gains were found in Peru when-issued papers, which traders attributed to the closing of Peru's restructuring deal expected in late February despite the continuing hostage crisis.
Traders paid scant attention to the issuance of DM125 million synthetic sovereign bond backed by Ecuador PDI.
One trader noted that Ecuador PDI's recent gains had been tied to the expected deal and interest in PDI waned once the structured deal was launched.
Just about all the news out of Latin America had been positive, said Suhas Ketkar, head of Latin America research at CS First Boston.
"Regional growth is good and inflation is low," he said, predicting that the inflation would be under 10 percent in 1997, the lowest since 1969.
Traders said Brazil outperformed Argentina on Thursday, reversing recent trends.
Brazil C eased 1/8 to 75-1/2, while Argentina FRBs lost 1/2 to 88-3/4 7.
